qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Qualified fab consumables (CMP pads, slurries, and advanced packaging materials) integrated into proprietary semiconductor fab recipes. High switching barriers as materials represent <1-2% of wafer cost but carry catastrophic yield-loss risk upon failure. Strong pricing power and high tangible ROIC (>25%), though legacy M&A goodwill from DuPont/Laird depresses GAAP ROIC to ~6.7%.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 4 (CAP = 5, REJECT). Semiconductor Materials Tier 3 baseline (10-15Y) receives a severe haircut to CAP=5 under Macrotrend [3] (Geopolitical Realignment & Supply Chain Reshoring). Fab customer demand is heavily concentrated in Taiwan (TSMC) and East Asian foundries subject to intensifying US-China export controls and cross-border trade friction, alongside severe wafer-start cyclicality.
qualitative.evidence: Spun off from DuPont in November 2025 as a standalone electronics materials company. While CMP consumables benefit from high customer switching costs and operating/tangible ROIC exceeds 25-40%, 5-year median GAAP ROIC is only 6.7% due to $8.6B in legacy goodwill and intangibles. Saddled with $4.1B in debt at separation (LT Debt/NI > 5.6x). Business model faces severe structural headwinds from semiconductor fab concentration in Taiwan/East Asia, geopolitical export bans, and wafer start volatility.
